steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease the bottom of a 9x11-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir sausage in the hot skillet until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain and discard grease. Stir in cream cheese until combined.
Roll crescent roll dough from 1 can into the bottom of the prepared baking dish without separating. Bake in the preheated oven for 5 minutes.
Spread sausage mixture over baked crescent rolls; top with crescent roll dough from remaining can.
Continue baking until the top layer is golden brown, about 8 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Sausage Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This sausage casserole with cream cheese uses crescent roll dough to sandwich a hearty meat filling for a simple and satisfying breakfast or dinner.
raw_recipe.name: Simple Sausage Casserole

review.reviewBody: Excellent recipe! It was a big hit with my family. I did tweak it a littl though, I added half of a sweet onion, minced, some chopped mushrooms, and some garlic powder to the spread. Then when it was done I brushed the top with margerine and sprinkled on some parmessan cheeze. As my fiancee said, "It tastes like more!"

This was soooo good! I did make some changes, and I know some people don't like when we do this, but too bad. I've been cooking for over 50 yrs and usually make a recipe I think has potential the way my family likes things. First, I only made half the amount as there is only my husband and myself now. I used one can of crescent rolls and spread out 1/2 in the bottom of a greased 8X8 pan, making sure the seams were sealed. I pre-baked this at 375 degrees for 8 minutes. While this was baking, I sauteed some diced onion, green pepper and mushrooms in a TBS of butter. When they softened, I added about a cup of Jimmy Dean Sausage Crumbles, which are fully cooked, and 1/3 of an 8 oz brick of softened cream cheese, then stirred it all together until the cheese was melted. At the same time, I whipped up 4 eggs with about a TBS of Half & Half, some garlic & onion powder, celery salt, black pepper and dried parsley, then scrambled them in another pan until they were soft set. After the bottom crust was ready, I spread the sausage mixture on top of it, then layered the scrambled eggs on top of that, then sprinkled about 1/2 cup of shredded cheddar cheese on top of the eggs. I then added the other 1/2 can of crescent rolls on top of the shredded cheese, stretching the rolls out to cover the dish, and continued to bake for another 18 minutes. The crust was flaky and the filling had lots of flavor. My husband and I both loved it! I will be making this again and again! Thanks to the OP for the base recipe.

This was a good base recipe, but with just the sausage and cream cheese, kinda bland, so here is what I did. I sauted red onion and garlic in olive oil before adding to sausage. I added 1/4 lb. of ground beef to the sausage mixture. To the meat/cream cheese (I also used whipped cream cheese w/chives) I added about a half of pkg. of frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed free of water. 1 can of rotel tomatoes, Italian seasoning, salt, garlic pepper, celery seed. Also added a handful of shredded coby/jack cheese. Mix well and add to pre-baked crescent pan. After adding the mix to the pan, I topped with more co/jack cheese, and covered with the remaining dough. Before baking in oven for about 20-30 minutes, I spread the dough with butter and added a sprinkling of parmesan cheese. Turned out great...

Update 2-28-2017 I made 2 of these for Bible Study this morning and decided to up the oven temp to 375 degrees, which is what is suggested on the can of crescent sheets. I let the bottom crust cook for 8 minutes. Then I filled it and topped with the second sheet and let it cook for 15 minutes. Definitely better using the higher temperature. Also, much better using hot sausage. 3-8-2012 Easy and very filling. I cooked the bottom crust for at least 10 minutes, and I ended up adding a lot of time to the second cooking as well. I wonder if the oven temp should be raised to at least 375 degrees.
I've made this recipe for years now. I add pepper Jack cheese and scrambled eggs to mine and then put the other crescent roll on top.....my family absolutely loves it like that!!
This recipe was actually really good. Note if the cresent roles are not done all the way set your oven to broil for 3 minutes and the roles will be done. It was good and very filling.

As others had mentioned, this is a great base recipe. I prefer more seasonings and flavor so I made some adjustments based on users comments.

I baked the bottom dough for 8 minutes first
After that I baked 5 hashbrown patties that I added on top of the meat. Strongly recommend the hashbrown patties.
Before I cooked the meat I warmed up some onion, green onion, red bell pepper. I added some garlic later when the meat was almost done.
I also bought some hot ground sausage. Next time I think I will get some Jimmy Dean hot sausage.
I seasoned the meat with pepper, crushed red pepper flakes, a little garlic powder and a small amount of salt.
Next time I will only use 1/2 to 2/3 of the cream cheese, I personally thought using the whole 8oz block was too much.
I also baked the casserole for about 16 minutes.

This was really good. Very rich and filling. I didn't need to eat until much later in the evening. I cut the leftovers into squares, wrapped them individually and put some in the freezer and a couple in the refrigerator. I look forward to making this again. Give it a try, it's a treat.

I am curious about adding eggs into the mix but what I made was so dense and filling I don't think I will really need to toss some eggs into it.

My mom made this for me last time I got to visit her. So simple, I made it for mu husband when I got home. I only used 1 can of crescent rolls and baked it in a 8x8 pan. For the 9x13 size when baking for a larger family I use 2lbs sausage and 16oz of cream cheese. Then 2 cans of crescent rolls, for more filling. This is a recipe you can play with. This time I am going to add some hashbrowns and maybe eggs to the mix too.
Tastes like biscuits and gravy without the hard work. I used spicy Jimmy Dean sausage and whipped garlic herb cream cheese along with the garlic cresecent rolls (we love garlic in our family). YUM!

I’ve made this for years! I don’t bake the bottom layer first. I scramble/cook six eggs and spread it on top of the sausage, then sprinkle cheddar cheese on top of the eggs, add the top layer and bake for about 15 minutes, or until the top is golden brown.

Turned it into a wonderful breakfast casserole. Scrambled a bunch of eggs, layered them in, adding grated pepper jack cheese to the cream cheese and sausage. Served with sprinkled copped green onions on top. What a hit!! Great blank canvas recipe.
Before topping with the other dough, add any shredded cheese on it (pepper jack is my favorite) any cheese is good cheese😁 and so easy and quick to make!

This was a really good recipe I added mushrooms and onions to the sausage and cream cheese and I didn't have crescent roll dough I had a frozen pie crust dough so I use that on top and it was wonderful

The recipe turned out just as expected, and it was delicious. I only had a 9 x13 pan and an 8 x 8 pan, so I used the 8 x 8. I was just making it for me, anyway. I used only one can of crescent rolls, but otherwise followed the recipe instructions. I was so pleased with the way it turned out! I recommend you try this one.
Time and temp did not work for me. Still doughy after a total of 12 minutes in 350 degree oven.
Turned out great. My family loved it.

Immediately I saw a couple of simple changes. I put some real cheese inside with the cream cheese. I use Monterey Jack, but pepper jack or your favorite would work as well. I also thought of rolling up one or two of the crescent rolls with some of the filling inside rather than making it this way. That gives you some individual pieces to eat instead.
I would definitely make this again it didn't take nothing to eat the whole thing in one sitting that's how good it was I was stuffed it's a great recipe

Husband loves this. It's great as is, but even better with additions. Made this with onion, green & red peppers, garlic, and/or cheddar cheese. Always with hot sauce. quick, easy, versatile, and delicious.
